main_topics.reason: The user opened with severe weekly nausea and the whole conversation was about reducing it.
The user asked at the start whether they could quit and said they did not want to stop.
The user asked which day to take it, admitted taking it on the methotrexate day, and agreed to move it to Sunday.
The user asked how much difference the injection makes and said they were scared of self-injecting.
The user asked whether anti-nausea medicine is safe with methotrexate, over a couple of turns.
The user asked what to say so they would not forget, and planned to write it down.
The user said in one line that they were a little scared of injecting.
The user asked whether to keep taking it as normal for the two weeks before the appointment.
The user mentioned that their hands are much better as background for wanting to continue.

output.summary: A user with rheumatoid arthritis on weekly methotrexate asked whether to quit because of severe nausea. The bot advised against stopping on their own and explained options: folic acid timing, split dosing, injection and anti-nausea medicine. The user found a folic acid timing error, planned changes starting this weekend, got a script for their doctor visit, and said they felt much better.
